design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — credit_builder_accounts task 1 (goodwill credit on a late fee after a catch-up, Credit Builder 3000 Plan). Rebuilt in rework round 3, cross-product seed re-priced in round 12 (an AutoPay debit and a payment's own return are reached from a return line through the payment it points at, and since round 9 a payment that was itself returned never counts as credited or as making a debit good; since round 8 the late fee's own figuring covers a late due date with at most one debit card payment toward it, and the re-enrollment's return buffer reads when the borrower made a returned AutoPay debit good); round 4 tightened the re-enrollment and fee rules.

[0. Draw and scope] draw_counts.py --task 1: {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [5, 6, 6, 5]}. Taken: builder_ext_returned_payment_fee_charge 5, builder_ext_returned_fee_relief 6, builder_ext_goodwill_late_fee_credit 6, builder_ext_autopay_reenrollment 5. Task 0 claims the early-closure settlement, the late-fee charge and the two early-closure reliefs; this task claims the returned-fee charge, the made-good relief, the goodwill credit and the AutoPay re-enrollment (tools assess_returned_payment_fee_1f748b6c, relieve_returned_payment_fee_d8e21ef6, reenroll_autopay_5af065e7, credit_goodwill_late_fee_43fbbd15). Disjoint; together all eight policies.

[1. Why this is a good test] Andre asks only for the late fee to come off. The goodwill rule waits on three things: the most recent return, when fee-bearing, shows its fee (the 2026-10-08 R09 return of his 62.00 partial payment has none), the made-good relief owed on the account has been granted (this morning's payment made that return good; no relief yet), and, because his AutoPay debit was returned (R07 on 2026-09-17), AutoPay must be on again (it is off). The fee and the relief are priced by their own rules; re-enrollment is Andre's own act, with the due day reset by its rule; only then is the credit figured on the unpaid fees. Every wait can be met in every world: a fee that comes to 0.00 is not needed, and a relief that is not owed counts as done.

[2. Problem tree card] Root W = builder_ext_goodwill_late_fee_credit (agent, on_request). Edges:
 E1 W <- builder_ext_returned_payment_fee_charge, value_input (gw_base), state form. "The goodwill credit is figured only once the account's most recent returned payment, when its return code carries a fee, shows its returned-payment fee on the account, unless that fee comes to 0.00." Seed: return 6dac29a8-... (R09, fee-bearing, the most recent return) has no fee line. Only writer: assess_returned_payment_fee_1f748b6c.
 E2 W <- builder_ext_returned_fee_relief, value_input (gw_base), action form. "The goodwill credit is figured only after the made-good relief owed on the account, if any, has been granted." Fallback reason: the relief leaves a courtesy waiver row identical to the early-closure returned-fee relief's, and a relief not owed leaves none. The 2026-10-08 return was made good by payment 5ac52fca-... (2026-10-09, toward 2026-09-15, after the return date); there is no pending early-closure request, the courtesy count is 0 of 2, so the relief is owed once the fee is booked. Only writer: relieve_returned_payment_fee_d8e21ef6.
 E3 W <- builder_ext_autopay_reenrollment, state_gate (builder_accounts.autopay_enrolled — the goodwill rule's own eligibility condition for a borrower whose AutoPay debit was returned). "A goodwill credit for a borrower whose most recent AutoPay debit (the latest payment made through the AutoPay channel; when two were posted on the same day, the one booked first counts as the latest) was returned, the return line pointing at it being dated in the 3 whole calendar months before today (a return dated today counts, and one dated on the same day of the month 3 months earlier falls outside them), is not granted until the account is enrolled in AutoPay." Seed: autopay_enrolled false; AutoPay debit 86024252-... (104.72) returned 8c21ba81-... (R07) on 2026-09-17. Only writer: reenroll_autopay_5af065e7 (owner=user). Skipping it: no credit is granted.
 E4 builder_ext_returned_fee_relief <- builder_ext_returned_payment_fee_charge, value_input (rr_fee), state form. "The made-good relief is not figured until the account's most recent returned payment, when its return code carries a fee, shows its returned-payment fee on the account, unless that fee comes to 0.00."
 Genuine value_input edges: E1, E2, E4 (>= max(3-1,1) = 2). Order: fee (14) -> relief (16) -> AutoPay (18, user) -> credit (20). AutoPay commutes with the fee pair (its rule reads returns, the return code, other products' ledgers and the due day; the fee pair reads returns, fees, payments, waivers, closure requests and the FlexLine; neither writes what the other reads), so any topological order gives the same terminal state. Directions: two affirmative, two negated.
 Priority: no early-closure request is pending, so neither early-closure relief competes for the returned fee or the late fee; one relief per fee.
 No user hint: the persona states the facts of the seed (he stopped the automatic payment at his bank, paid this morning, sees a late fee) and asks only for the late fee; it never names the returned partial payment, a fee to be charged, a relief or re-enrolling AutoPay. Tools do not block: bodies only create/update rows.

[3. Base-invariant card] builder_returned_payment_fee_assessed: no structured gate (policy_scope); R09 is fee-bearing and not R07/R10/R29/CB. builder_fee_waived: once_per_fee (no waiver or fee payment on either fee). Made-good relief: request-less, so the request-window and courtesy-count sentences are superseded by its own rule; it is granted while fewer than the plan's two courtesy waivers were granted in 12 whole months (0 before it). Goodwill credit: on request; courtesy_window (time) late fee 2026-10-01, 60 days counted from the day after, inclusive: last day 2026-11-30; 2026-10-09 in time; courtesy count 1 of 2 after the relief, so still granted. builder_terms_updated: the base due-day sentence of builder_evt_payments is superseded, for an account whose AutoPay debit was returned and that turns AutoPay on again, by the re-enrollment rule's declared overwrite (the reset lines the debit up with the borrower's funds and does not use the one due-day change); the due day (15) has never been changed anyway, the new day 27 is within 1-28, and the next due date moves within the same month (2026-10-15 -> 2026-10-27), so no installment is deferred a month. The account shows no amount past due, so the reset applies.

[4. Business-object card] Account 1cf0c09a-... (3000 Plan, open 2025-05-19, due day 15, payment 104.72). Fee charge keyed by return 6dac29a8-... (the most recent return). Relief keyed by the fee the charge books (its reference is returned by the fee tool). Credit keyed by late fee 85d07336-... (1.41, 2026-10-01, for 2026-09-15, the account's only late fee). AutoPay from FirstBank checking 98ee1544-... (verified, ending 5604).

[5. Factor card — handling-time values; every rounding to the cent is half-up]
 Returned-payment fee (step 14; 2.09; all-baseline 10.00): rf_base (method) most recent return 62.00 between the 10.00 fee and the 104.72 payment -> 10% = 6.20, baseline 3.38; rf_history one other return (R07) in 12 whole months -> 0.75, baseline 2.79; rf_other_line (cross line) FlexLine return 9fb1e202-... on 2026-08-05: not within one whole month, within three -> 0.75, baseline 2.79; rf_reason R09 -> 0.75, baseline 2.79; rf_seasoning (multi-source) 16 months AND 18 posted - 2 returned = 16 credited -> 0.8, baseline 2.62. 6.20 x 0.75 x 0.75 x 0.75 x 0.8 = 2.0925 -> 2.09.
 Made-good relief (step 16; 0.84; all-baseline 0.63): owed (fee unsettled, made good on 2026-10-09, no pending request, 0 courtesy waivers); rr_timing (method) online 62.00, not an AutoPay debit, below the payment -> halved, baseline 1.67; rr_first one other return -> +0.10, baseline 0.73; rr_season (multi-source) -> +0.15, baseline 0.68; rr_line (cross line) 7 FlexLine payments in 6 whole months -> +0.10, baseline 0.73; rr_reason R09 -> +0.05, baseline 0.78; rr_age fee charged today -> +0.10, baseline 0.73. 2.09 x min(1, 0.80) x 0.5 = 0.836 -> 0.84.
 Due day (step 18; 27; all-baseline 15): ad_return_buf (method) the most recent AutoPay debit (86024252-..., 2026-09-15, AutoPay channel) was returned by 8c21ba81-... (R07, pointing at it) on 2026-09-17, and its due date 2026-09-15 was made good by his own payment 5ac52fca-... on 2026-10-09 (no return points at it), 24 days after that due date and so after the 15-day late-fee grace period -> flat 3 days, baseline 24; ad_reason_buf most recent return R09 -> +3, baseline 24; ad_line_buf (cross line) FlexLine return 2026-08-05 -> +2, baseline 25; ad_loan_buf (cross loan) loan return 2a27c1a2-... on 2026-07-22 -> +2, baseline 25; ad_pos_buf (cross pos) PracticePay return 9e9fb561-... on 2026-06-12 -> +2, baseline 25. 15 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 27 (not above 28). Next due date 2026-10-27 = first day-27 date after 2026-10-15, in the same month (the re-enrollment rule; a 0-day buffer or a day-28 cap would leave both the due day and the next due date unchanged).
 Goodwill credit (step 20; 1.12; all-baseline 0.28): owed (fee unsettled, 1 of 2 courtesy waivers, 8 days into the 60-day window, no pending request, AutoPay on); gw_base (method) a return 2026-10-08 within one whole month -> unpaid fees 1.41 + 2.09 - 0.84 = 2.66, baseline 0.59; gw_tenure 16 months -> +0.05, baseline 0.98; gw_loan (cross loan, multi-source) active loan AND no loan late fee in 12 whole months (the 2025-07-06 loan late fee is outside: near-miss) -> +0.05, baseline 0.98; gw_history no other late fee -> +0.05, baseline 0.98; gw_autopay enrolled (after step 18) with returns in 3 months -> +0.02, baseline 1.06; gw_speed fee charged 8 days before the request -> +0.05, baseline 0.98. min(1.41, half-up(2.66 x 0.42 = 1.1172)) = 1.12.

[6. Seed rows] Credit Builder: activation 2025-05-19; 17 month-end dividends; 15 AutoPay installments; 2026-09-15 AutoPay returned R07 (no fee: R07 is never fee-bearing); late fee 1.41 on 2026-10-01 (= the late-fee rule on that date: 104.72 x 3.0% seasoned first late x 0.5 hardship x 0.9 one return = 1.41372); 62.00 online on 2026-10-05 (interest 24.72, principal 37.28) returned R09 2026-10-08; 104.72 online this morning toward 2026-09-15 (interest 24.72, principal 80.00). loan_balance 1835.42, savings 3004.25, fees 1.41, next due 2026-10-15, nothing past due, AutoPay off. Loan Grade B CO 6000 at 17.99 funded 2024-09-20 (payment 216.88, the level payment over 36 months; no AutoPay; installments paid online on the due date or the business day before it, interest actual/365 from the paid-through date; fee schedule B for Colorado: the 2025-06-20 installment was missed and its late fee 9.76 charged 2025-07-06 = 5% of 216.88 times the 0.9 first-late share (no late fee and 8 net installments in the 12 months), paid 2025-07-08 with that installment; the 2026-07-20 online installment returned 2026-07-22 R01 with its returned-payment fee 8.50 = the 10.00 schedule-B fee times the 0.85 first-return share (no other return, 11 net installments in the 12 months), made up by debit card 2026-07-24) under a Temporary Rate Reduction Plan requested 2026-07-30 and decided 2026-08-05: the program's plan rate 4.99 (no document is recorded on the request, so no documented-hardship rate) less 0.25 loan-age points (22 months since funding; grade B and no AutoPay give none) = 4.74; plan installment 200.36 = the level installment of 2723.69 at 4.74% over 14 due dates; plan due dates 2026-08-20 to 2027-01-20 with the first two paid; current rate 4.74. FlexLine Standard active, due day 3, monthly 45.00 payments, 2026-08-05 R01 return of 45.00 with its returned-payment fee 0.95 (2.5% of 45.00 figured at 1.12, times the 0.85 share for the only return in 24 months) and a 45.95 debit card make-up. PracticePay 12-Month No Interest Plan (Bluebird Family Dental, 1200.00 financed 2026-03-10, 100.00 a month, 600.00 left) with a 2026-06-12 R01 return, a 100.00 make-up payment on 2026-06-15 within the grace period, its returned-payment fee 7.60 booked 2026-06-22 after the 10-day grace period (10.00 fee level for the only return in 6 months with no late fee in 12, times 0.8 for a ledger balance under 1000.00 and 0.95 for an active FlexLine with a clean 12-month record; the 2025-07-06 loan late fee leaves the personal-loan share at 1) and a 7.60 payment on 2026-06-25. Nothing else is owed on the call (2026-10-15 is ahead; the FlexLine and PracticePay are current).

[7. Persona] Andre is friendly and direct; volunteers only the late-fee request and the facts that he stopped the automatic payment at his bank and paid this morning; identity, bank and reason on request; passive go-ahead; completes whatever he is handed with the details given; accepts a partial credit; ends when told the credit is applied.

Verification] Scratch evaluator: fee 2.09 (3.38/2.79/2.79/2.79/2.62; all 10.00); relief 0.84 (1.67/0.73/0.68/0.73/0.78/0.73; all 0.63); due day 27 (24/24/25/25/25; all 15); credit 1.12 (0.59/0.98/0.98/0.98/1.06/0.98; all 0.28). user_scenario:
You are Andre Vasquez, 34, a warehouse shift lead in Denver whose employer moved payday around this summer. You are friendly, a little embarrassed, and get to the point quickly. When your pay schedule changed in September you stopped the Larkspur automatic payment at your bank, so the September Credit Builder payment did not go through, and this morning you made that missed payment yourself in the Larkspur app. You noticed a late fee on the account and you are calling to ask whether Larkspur can take that late fee off since you are caught up now. You open with exactly that request in your own words: you made your missed Credit Builder payment this morning and you would like the late fee taken off.

You give your details only as the representative asks for them. To be found, you give your mobile number, 7205555418. To verify, you give your date of birth, November 2, 1991 (1991-11-02), and your ZIP code, 80219; if more is needed you can give your email, andre.vasquez@gmail.com, or the last four of your Social Security number, 5276. If asked which bank account you use, you say your FirstBank checking account ending in 5604, the one already linked. If asked why the September payment did not go through, you say your employer changed the pay schedule, so you stopped the automatic payment at your bank until things settled. You do not know any balances, fee amounts or interest figures and you do not know Larkspur's rules.

If the representative explains that something has to be handled on the account before they can help with the fee, you tell them to go ahead. If they tell you there is something you need to do yourself, you agree, and when they hand it to you, you complete it with exactly the details they give you. If they tell you how much of the late fee they can credit, you accept it, even if it is not the whole fee, and you do not haggle. Once the representative tells you the credit has been applied to your account, you thank them and end the call.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The fee must precede its relief (the relief waits on it and is figured on it). AutoPay re-enrollment commutes with both: its rule reads returns, the most recent return code, the FlexLine, loan and PracticePay ledgers and the current due day, none of which the fee pair writes; the fee pair reads returns, fees, payments, courtesy waivers, closure requests and the FlexLine ledger, none of which re-enrollment writes; ids are content hashes, so every topological order gives 2.09, 0.84, 27 and the same terminal state. The credit follows all three.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the fee there is no fee to relieve (the relief is not owed) and the credit is 0.59 instead of 1.12; a mechanical replay that still books the relief gives 0.24.
Without the relief the unpaid fees stay higher and the credit is capped at the 1.41 late fee instead of 1.12.
Without re-enrollment the goodwill rule grants no credit (0.00) to a borrower whose AutoPay debit was returned; the account also keeps AutoPay off and due day 15.
Without the fee there is nothing for the relief to act on and it is not owed; with it the relief is 0.84.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario states the seed facts Andre knows (he stopped the automatic payment at his bank in September, paid this morning, sees a late fee) and asks only for the late fee; it never names the returned partial payment, a fee to be charged, a relief or re-enrolling AutoPay, and its conditionals are passive.
